title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : A **Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard** are two unique Soul items in *Dark Souls*. They are used by the Chosen Undead to partially satiate the Lordvessel together with two full Lord Souls, and gain access to the Kiln of the First Flame.

The Four Kings and Seath the Scaleless each own a Bequeathed Shard, which differ in lore from Lord Souls as they are only fragments of Gwyn's own Lord Soul, although even these fragments remain immensely powerful.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : Both the Four Kings and Seath the Scaleless drop a Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard upon their defeat.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - backstory 
 backstory : Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards differ from Lord Souls in that they are shards of the Lord Soul of Gwyn. The owners of these shards were awarded them because Gwyn recognized the talent of the Four Kings of New Londo as leaders, and because Seath aided the Lords in the war of the Dragons.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the term (Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, thus stating how Seath had become part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet: **While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift thus allowing the dragon a more close connection to the family of the monarch.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Transitioning from its disguised to active state will take some time and is a perfect opportunity to finish it off if the player is capable of dealing enough damage.
If one is patient enough, it is possible to observe a Mimic breathing and moving slightly as their idle animation. They'll even stretch their arms and legs out in rare occurrences.
Throwing a Lloyd's Talisman at a Mimic will cause it to open its mouth, allowing players to safely retrieve items from it without having to fight it. This can be done even if the mimic is hostile, in which case it'll sit back down.
It used to be possible to kill every Mimic in the game and not get the Symbol of Avarice. However, Patch 1.05 made the final Mimic in The Duke's Archives (the one in front of the exit to the grove of Crystal Golems) a guaranteed source for a Symbol of Avarice upon killing it.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Mimics disguise themselves as chests, waiting for victims to try to open them. When a player attempts to do so, Mimics will proceed to chomp on them in a special grab move, causing heavy damage.

If Mimics are hurt before they can grab a player, they reveal a large, lolling tongue and lines of finger-bone teeth, followed by the arms and legs. Once upright they will begin to aggressively pursue their prey. Mimics are fast, tough, and deal high damage; they can easily kill the unprepared.

In order to determine the difference between a Mimic and Chest, the most direct visual cue one can get is by looking at the chain connected to the right side of the chest. If the chain is wrapped in a circle then the chest is safe, if the chain is straightened out then it's a Mimic. The mimic chest will also do a long, slow breath with its lid slightly rising up and down once every 17 seconds.

title: Mimic
snippet:
In Co-op it is actually possible to save another player from a mimic. When the other player opens the mimic, if one acts quickly and attacks the mimic while it is still opening, it will instead stand up and initiate normal combat.
Mimics can't climb ladders.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - locations 
 locations : A total of nine Mimics can be encountered in the game:

In a chamber that contains an elevator going up to the control room.

Guarded by two Sentinels in the room left of the first bonfire.
In a dark room behind an illusory wall near the third bonfire. The room where Havel's Set is found.
Two on the upper floor area near the spiral staircase.
The Duke's Archives ×2
On an upper balcony area, guarded by two Undead Crystal Soldiers just before encountering Seath the Scaleless for the first time.
In a small library, near the exit leading to the garden area of the archives.
Oolacile Township ×2
On the roof of a circular tower, in plain sight
Inside a stone building past the circular tower. Second floor. Rolling is needed to reach it.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : The mimic originates in the original *Advanced Dungeons & Dragons* *Monster Manual* (1977). In that sourcebook, they are carnivorous shapechangers able to take the form of any solid stone or wooden object, though they are most commonly depicted as treasure chests. Mimics have since appeared in numerous video game RPGs.
**According to *Dungeons & Dragons* editor Tim Kask, Gary Gygax created the mimic to foil players who checked for traps before opening treasure chests. The result, just as in Dark Souls, was to instill a sense of paranoia among players opening chests.
A Mimic's teeth are actually finger bones.
Mimics have a unique death animation if they die before being awakened.
If the player watches closely, a Mimic lying in wait will slowly open its lid, and then slowly close it.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - attacks

† Only applies when opening a Mimic.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : These creatures were once part of the great clan of the Gods but at one point they committed the sin of "greed". For this they were banished and cursed, resulting into their heads transforming into an imitation of treasure chests. They would became known as Mimics and spread across the world, simulating chests to trick and devour adventurers or becoming deadly defense mechanisms to protect peculiar artifacts.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Mimics** are special enemies encountered in *Dark Souls*. They will initially remain on the same spot, non-hostile and disguised as item chests until the player either opens them, which triggers a strong special grab, or hits them, which turns them hostile. There is a fixed number of nine Mimics found throughout the game, always in the same spots.

The usually-valuable treasure they contain can be obtained by either opening them safely using a Lloyd's Talisman or killing them. They do not respawn when killed, and in all versions of the game post Patch 1.05, the Mimic located in the Duke's Archives always drops the previously-rare Symbol of Avarice headware upon death.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - theory 
 theory : It's possible that the curse "imposed" to them is actually a mutation caused by their greed

The Gaping Dragon, the Crow Demons, the Covetous Demon, and many other beings attest that strong emotions can warp one's body. It's therefore plausible that the Mimic were molded by greed, and that their mutation had been attributed to divine punishment due to a mistaken interpretation.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategies 
 strategies : A good way to quickly dispatch a Mimic is to land as much damage before it is fully upright. Using attacks such as the two handed leaping attack or a powerful spell is the best way to weaken it as much as possible due to the long transformation.
When the mimic is active, it will move quickly and deal high damage if it hits. In particular, its spinning kick deals high knockback and damage.
If a Mimic is able to start chewing on the player, the player is most assuredly going to die. However, rapidly pressing the weak attack buttons will allow the player to escape.
All of the Mimic's attacks except for the standing kick, which must either be blocked or dodged, will miss if the player positions him/herself close against the Mimic.
Once a Mimic is awake, Lloyd's Talismans can still lull them, allowing the player to heal themselves or finish it off.

Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics

Moonlight Greastsword raises magic defense by 40 points and cannot be Enchanted.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : The Moonlight Greatsword is the *Dark Souls* interpretation of the Moonlight Sword, which has appeared in every From Software game since *King's Field*.
The Moonlight Greatsword is one of the four Dragon weapons that has a parameter bonus (the others being Priscilla's Dagger, Dragon Bone Fist and the Dragon Tooth).

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - description 
 description : This sword, one of the rare dragon weapons, came from the tail of Seath the Scaleless, the pale white dragon who betrayed his own.

Seath is the grandfather of sorcery, and this sword is imbued with his magic, which shall be unleashed as a wave of moonlight.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - lead 
 lead : The **Moonlight Greatsword** is a greatsword in *Dark Souls*.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls)
snippet: A very popular weapon for intensive Intelligence builds due to its high scaling. Its strong attack (be it one-handed or two-handed) releases a magic-based projectile that deals damage based on the Intelligence of the player, though it depletes some of its durability (20 per use one-handed, 40 per use two-handed), it's a very powerful attack with the right investment into Intelligence. The Moonlight Greatsword's projectile will go through enemies that block it, potentially hitting a wall and exploding, hitting through the block and dealing full damage.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - upgrades 
 upgrades : Interestingly, the Moonlight Greatsword +5 swings slightly faster than the Standard Moonlight Greatsword.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Eons past his demise, the soul of the Paledrake remanifested in Drangleic, albeit in a lessened form, and possessed a mere spider. Its shape and condition notwithstanding, the obsession within "the Writhing Ruin", as it came to be known, led the spider to doggedly seek out its desires. Namely, it sought its "home" deep inside the mines of Tseldora, the old crystal cave of Seath, and where the petrified corpse of an ancient archdragon was found, and made it into its lair.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The ghostly hands that emerge from the tomes in the Grand Archives in *Dark Souls III* closely resemble those of Seath; not only visually, but also functionally, as they cause curse build-up in those who come too close, similar to Seath's Curse Beam attacks.
Seath's character is an homage to the dragon god of the same name in FromSoftware's King's Field series for the original Playstation. The Souls series is often referred to as the spiritual successor to King's Field.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : When first encountered in The Duke's Archives, he regenerates health extremely quickly due to the power of Primordial Crystal, effectively making him invincible.. He inevitably kills the player. Loss of souls and humanity can be avoided by wearing a Ring of Sacrifice, but if he kills the player through Curse, then a Rare Ring of Sacrifice is needed to avoid penalties. In addition, it is possible to travel back through the fog door to avoid being killed by Seath, however can still go through the fog wall after exiting. Regardless, the player must be killed by Seath in order to progress.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath eventually sired a humanoid hybrid daughter, Shira. Although the mother is never stated explicitly, Shira is both "one whose veins coarse with royal blood", and a "descendant of Gods", making her likely mother Seath's spouse who was a relative of Gwyn.
 Shira became the sworn knight and personal handmaiden to Princess Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, and the two, together with the dragon Darkeater Midir, would be forever sent away to the Ringed City, the hidden city Gwyn gifted to the humans who helped him end the Age of Ancients, so that the three would keep the Dark within at bay. Shira would remain in the Ringed City for the rest of her life, dutifully guarding Filianore over countless ages, although she would always take pride in being Seath's daughter.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Another possible daughter of Seath was Crossbreed Priscilla, a half-dragon hybrid whose dragon attributes are reminiscent of him; as she is outright described as a bastard, she would have been conceived out of wedlock. Priscilla was feared by the other gods and treated as an abomination due to her Lifehunt powers and unnatural origin. Eventually she was drawn away into the cold and lonely Painted World of Ariamis, trapped within a great canvas.

Seath seemingly had little interest in politics or pleasure, choosing to immerse himself in research of the scales of immortality that the ancient dragons possessed but he lacked. His Archives became a magnificent pool of tomes and knowledge, the fruits of Seath's superior wisdom and unsound fixation over achieving the immortality that was denied to him at birth.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point, the Four Lords who had found immense Lord Souls and built their civilizations underground emerged to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world for themselves. Seath decided to betray his race to ally with Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and help the Lords in the war. He was instrumental in the gods' eventual victory, and the triumphant Lords would exterminate much of the Ancient Dragons, cementing their rule. Seath would also pillage the Ancient Dragons' sacred treasure, the Primordial Crystal, the centerpiece of his efforts to achieve immortality.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: maidens of Gwynevere, before Seath's experiments transformed them. Although Gwyndolin, as the last remaining deity in Anor Londo, did not punish him for this heinous act, Seath was confined to his Archives, declared a forbidden area and demarcated by a divine magical barrier, so that no one could approach the Archives. Meanwhile his Channelers, steadfast in their service of the Duke, continued their travels, kidnapping subjects for his experiments.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: infestation with satisfaction. The spider haunted by Seath thus returned to the depths of the mines next to the petrified body of the ancient dragon and began to accumulate the souls gathered in the lands of Tseldora, absorbing them from people until they grew immensely. Though Freja was ultimately slain, Tark was doubtful it would be the end of Seath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Following the death of their creator, multiple moon butterflies survived over the centuries, migrating to Drangleic and mutating into lesser Great Moths and developing poisoning abilities. They remained rare and mysterious creatures that appeared only on full-moon nights in winter, and whose larvae were never once spotted. Other creations of Seath that reached Drangleic included Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka: Two of Seath's many experiments on humans, the pale dragon's crossbreeding experiments had seemingly cursed their souls into being together. The two were well aware of being the product of Seath's madness and his obsessive attempt to achieve immortality.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Studying the sorceries and knowledge brought to the Archives by the Crystal Sages, Oceiros would find himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, one that led to enlightenment only to be followed by madness. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. His mad plans would find support from Pontiff Sulyvahn, who began experimenting with transforming humans into pale dragons. Despite the large number of failures and abominations that presented only a faded fragment of the dragons' strength, the experiments were eventually successful and Oceiros managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon resembling Seath, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the other deities abandoned Anor Londo and moved to an unknown location. Seath remained in his Archives, now completely estranged from the world and obsessed with his research.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Seath's research focused on souls, seeking ways to manipulate them and draw out the power within, mainly through sorcery. Seath, in possession of the Primordial Crystal, noticed the peculiar connection between crystals and souls, and the way in which this element could be used to best catalyze their power, as crystals represented an ideal medium to create a bond between souls and objects. Seath would thus pioneer the Crystal Sorceries, a powerful branch of sorcery. The revelation was the beginning of Seath's obsession with crystals, which became the focus of much of his experiments. He managed to create a Crystal Ember capable of infusing weapons with the power of the crystals and passed this knowledge on to the Giant Blacksmith of the gods.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
His only long range specific attack is the far curse beam. That means if players stay at a distance, one can lure him to fire the beam and charge his defenseless body.

Crystal curse explosion triggers when the player cannot be reached by any of Seath's other attacks; usually when situated behind Seath with the tails just out of reach. One strategy is to begin sprinting a good distance away from him once he arches forward to charge a ball of magic. A second approach would be to develop a high enough curse resistance and block some of the erupting crystals. Immediately heal the damage received before he executes his tail swipes/slams.

Being the grandfather of Sorcery, Seath is extremely resistant to Magic damage, so it would be wise to try to use a different element when combating him.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
However, the knowledge within the tomes, said to "[all too easily] wash away its inquirers' anchors of reason", posed a threat to the sanity of the scholars. The profound research into the nature of the soul that once drove Logan into madness was likely contained within the Archives. The "foulness" that permeated the books manifested physically as well, in the form of ghostly and pale limbs that attacked and cursed those who came too close.

In the final years of Lothric's kingdom, King Oceiros, frustrated by continuous failures to find a worthy Champion, turned to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives. Here he found the twisted worship of Seath, developing a fascination for the Pale Dragon and the secrets of his moonlight. His newfound devotion was testified by his dragonscale ring, which he claimed protected him from his enemies, and his army's usage of shields decorated with a white dragon.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Respawning at the prison bonfire is tied to the room and not dying to Seath. This means being killed by Seath while outside the room will not move the player to the prison.
**Similarly, if Big Hat Logan kills the player in this area they will be moved to the prison.
If the player cuts off Seath's tail it may not disappear and will persist after Seath has been killed.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: It should be noted that Seath takes extra damage if hit in his belly. As an example, when hit with standard 1H fast attack Man-serpent Greatsword +15 in of his tentacles at STR 40, Seath takes 226 damage. And if hit in his belly by the same attack, he will take about 450 damage. If the character is tanky enough and has enough Curse resistance, he can stay right at Seath's belly and hit him without pausing until Seath dies, using his Estus Flask only one or two times.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point the Crystal Sages reached Lothric and became the spiritual guides of the scholars of the Grand Archives. The Crystal Sages introduced to Lothric not only crystal gems but also the heretical belief in the pale dragon Seath and his mad knowledge. The sages would thus continue to work on their research within the Grand Archives, even taking Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild as their pupil, and crafting weapons and casting tools that used the power of crystals to enhance their magical power, representing how the fruits of the lifetime of research had advanced to an impressive level and still followed the works of the pale dragon. The Grand Archives would grow into an enormous structure housing volumes of research on Seath's crystal sorceries.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Through their successful alliance against the Everlasting Dragons, Seath became a close friend to the Lord of Sunlight and was amply rewarded for his indispensable contributions to the war. He was wed into Gwyn's family as his son-in-law, inducting him into the nobility of the Gods, and was bestowed the honorific of "Duke". Gwyn further gifted Seath a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the Royal Archives, an enormous library towering above Anor Londo, which contained all the knowledge available to the city of the gods, leaving the dragon the freedom to do his own research; in time, the archives became so synonymous with Seath that they became known as "The Duke's Archives" instead.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : , also known as **Duke Seath**, is a boss in *Dark Souls*. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II*, albeit only as the "**Paledrake**", and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*.

One of four great beings who must be slain in *Dark Souls* so that their special souls may satiate the Lordvessel, he uniquely has two distinct boss battles, each with a different location and moveset. In another unique occurence, the first one atop The Duke's Archives must result in the player's death for the game to progress, while he can actually be defeated in his true boss battle at the end of the Crystal Cave.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: You can also use fast spells to cut his tail. Unlike using weapons, it is recommended to retreat from the boss battle (Homeward, Homeward Bone, or quit game) if you fail to cut it on the first try after breaking the crystal.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : By the era of Lothric, Seath was still widely considered the "pale dragon" of legends even by the sorcerers of Vinheim, though his crystal sorceries were all but consigned to legend.

There were some who still upheld Seath's legacy: The Crystal Sages, twin scholars who considered themselves the spiritual successors of the legendary grand sage Logan, came to possess the Crystal Scroll containing the sorceries and research of the pale dragon, which lead to Logan's records of Crystal Sorcery. The two sages were thus able to carry on this branch of sorcery, allowing them to replicate Logan's discoveries that utilize the power of crystals to their fullest as a medium for souls thanks to his "enlightenment" in the Regal Archives of Seath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Upon encountering him again within the Crystal Cave, he will be fought within an arena that contains the Primordial Crystal. In order to defeat Seath, it is necessary to destroy the Primordial Crystal so that any damage dealt to him is not immediately healed. The crystal will respawn if the player dies or leaves the fight, making it necessary to destroy it in each attempt to defeat Seath.

Staying at his side makes it easier to stay out of the area-of-effect of his breath attacks, and he won't be able to hit with his claws or tail as easily. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DI022PgUq38%7CVideo Video]

It is also possible to use only a bow against Seath with great success. Get a good distance away from him and it is possible to get 4-5 shots in before he gets too close. The only real danger in this strategy is when running past Seath to gain some distance.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At the culmination of his quest, Seath was able to achieve what he had always sought: immortality through the Primordial Crystal. By connecting his body and soul to the powerful crystal, the pale dragon gained insulation from death, so that no mortal blow could affect him and his wounds would close promptly, as long as the crystal was intact. His very breath became a powerful crystal breath that emitted a lethal curse.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Seath is one of the primordial archdragons who inhabited the world when, before the appearance of the First Flame, the world was composed only of grey rocks.

Seath was born with unique characteristics compared to the other archdragons, lacking the rock scales that made his brethren immortal. In addition, Seath's pale and deformed body was infused with the magical power of moonlight, through the study of which he created weapons that catalyzed it.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - moonlight_greatsword 
 moonlight_greatsword : To cut off a tail it's necessary to deal a certain amount of damage against it. The HP of the tail increases with higher NG cycles and is based on the HP of the respective enemy. Seath's tail has 825 health on Ng and 1,295 on NG+.
Equipment load under 25% is highly recommended to cut his tail.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Being the grandfather of Sorcery, Seath is extremely resistant to Magic damage, so it would be wise to try to use a different element when combating him.

When trying to obtain the Moonlight Greatsword it is best to attack the tip of the tail, as the area around midway through the tail is considered his body. Thus dealing damage to this area will not help in acquiring the Moonlight Greatsword.

A good strategy for acquiring it is when Seath himself breaks the Primordial Crystal. Wait behind the crystal until Seath starts to rear up his head for any of the Curse Beam attacks. Just before he fires it, start sprinting left or right around the sides and towards his tail. Seath will break the crystal and stun himself, giving the player ample opportunity to attack his tail three to four times. Make sure Seath's tail isn't clipping in the wall before trying.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The pale dragon's experiments were successful in animating Crystal Golems with souls and infusing Undead Soldiers with crystals. To adequately supply his research, the cave that housed his Primordial Crystal was gradually crowded with crystals, nearly overtaking the Archive's inner gardens. Seath also created the soul of the Moonlight Butterflies, mystical creatures that emitted crystallic power and Seath's moonlight as sorceries. Seath also managed to crystallize his own magical power of moonlight, creating a Greatsword that catalyzed it.

As a nobleman on par with the gods, Seath also had personal servants. His Channelers, trained sorcerers that became his eyes, hands, and feet, would reach and see what the dragon could not, and helped him in his research. The Channelers wore outfits representing Seath, with the six eyes on their helms meant to "compensate for Seath's lack of sight"; the nature of his lack of sight, and when he became impaired, are unknown.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: The structures of Seath's Crystal Cave endured and "drifted" to settle underground in southern Drangleic, the power of the white dragon lingering on as radiance within the crystals. The crystals infused with the souls of Seath became known as "Brightstones" and the kingdom of Olaphis mined these gems, refining and polishing them to be incorporated into their staves and rings, used as amplifiers for their sorceries.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : Encountered at the top of The Duke's Archives, and later at the end of the Crystal Cave.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Centuries after the fall of Olaphis, the territory of the Brightstone mines came under the control of the Duchy of Tseldora. Under the reign of Vendrick, the Duke of Tseldora rediscovered the precious crystals and, starting to extract and sell them again, made a fortune with brightstone. The citizens of Tseldora flourished thanks to the gem trade, and accumulated luxuries as well as knowledge of witchcraft. However, Seath's obsession that radiated from these crystals would bewitch the town inhabitants with a burning desire, insatiated by the prosperity they acquired, always searching for something they lacked.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Equipment load under 25% is highly recommended to cut his tail.
Lure Seath as close as possible to the crystal. It is ideal to kite Seath close to one of the walls, so that when he attacks with his breath, you have plenty of room to move around his other side. Once Seath is close enough to you he will pause and begin his breath attack; immediately run behind Seath. Run to his left side (your right), as he breathes his crystal breath from his right to his left. Seath will destroy the crystal with his own breath attack and be stunned temporarily. Without locking on to him, target the tip of his back (middle) tail and attack it while two-handing your highest damage weapon or using fast strong spells.
Use weapons that have vertical slash when two-handed: katanas, straightswords, greatswords, ultra greatswords, etc. Slash the tip once or twice, then run away. Provoke him to attack with his crystal breath, run to his tail, slash once or twice again, then repeat.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
**Similarly, if Big Hat Logan kills the player in this area they will be moved to the prison.
If the player cuts off Seath's tail it may not disappear and will persist after Seath has been killed.
Although it is never explicitly said, it is possible to infer that the victory of the Lords over the Ancient Dragons occurred directly thanks to Seath, through him revealing that the weakness of his race was lightning, capable of piercing their stone Dragon Scales. This is because in the Japanese version of the Opening, it is explained how the Lords' victory was "caused" by Seath's betrayal (ウロコのない白竜、シースの裏切りにより、遂に古竜は敗れた TL: And because of the betrayal of the scaleless white dragon Seath, the ancient dragons were finally defeated). This would also explain the immense amount of gifts that Gwyn gave to the white dragon including the Archives of the Gods, a political position in his empire, a woman from his family and a fragment of his Lord's soul.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: The Duke of Tseldora, continuing to mine the brightstone, discovered the stone body of the archdragon, as well as the spider possessed by Seath's soul. He eventually built his hidden chamber among the ruins deep within the mines, amassing a large library and conducting research on sorcery. Since he was an oddball who loved and was fascinated by spiders, the Duke eventually found the one possessed by Seath and decided to take it in as his pet, naming it "Freja" and locking it in a cage in the library where he led his studies. "Freja" eventually escaped from her cage and the numerous Parasite Spiders of its lair began to swarm the town of Tseldora, overrunning it and taking control of the bodies of their inhabitants as their hosts, while the Duke, driven mad, simply remained to gaze at their infestation with satisfaction. The spider haunted by Seath thus returned to the depths of the mines next to the petrified body of the ancient dragon and began to accumulate the souls gathered in the

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the Chinese term (Pinyin: *wàiqì*, Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, indicating that Seath became part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.
**While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift, establishing a closer relation between the dragon and the royal family.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Although the white dragon achieved his prized immortality, the arduous process had consumed him. The loneliness within him, the bane of his existence since his conception as a malformed dragon, was only fueled by the countless hours wiled away in solitude seeking his "cure"; the void within him was tragically left unfulfilled. The power and status he had since attained remained hollow, against the envy and resentment he harbored first towards his brethren, and then the world at large. His experiments grew more and more twisted as the inescapable reality of his condition drove him insane. The Archives were soon reduced to a prison housing the abominations of Seath such as the Serpent-men, unwitting jailers of volumes of scientific works, and the Pisaca, serpentine women who were once holy maidens of Gwynevere, before Seath's experiments transformed them. Although Gwyndolin, as the last remaining deity in Anor Londo, did not punish him for this heinous act, Seath was confined to his

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : In the region and times of Drangleic, Seath's name had been forgotten, merely referred to as an "Old One"; the legend of a pale dragon was nonetheless passed on in various locales, even if each account was fragmentary. His Moonlight Sword that shone like the brilliant rays of the moon and was born from his white being had become a thing of the oldest legends, rarely spoken of. The smithing techniques of Seath that used souls to create artifacts were preserved by a clan of Crow Demons, though they remembered the dragon only as a white grotesque being that existed in the distant past.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: When a Chosen Undead was able to ring the Bells of Awakening, overcome the challenges of Sen's Fortress and reach Anor Londo thus being rewarded with the Lordvessel, they would be guided by Kingseeker Frampt to find immense souls to fill the receptacle, and link the fading First Flame to succeed Gwyn in his sacrifice. The Chosen Undead would reach the Duke's Archives, where they were initially defeated and imprisoned by the immortal dragon. Managing to escape, the Chosen Undead would cross the dangerous Archives and reach the Crystal Cave where the Primordial Crystal was kept, source of the pale dragon's invulnerability. Seath would soon arrive at the cave to defend his crystal, but following the crystal's destruction would be slain by the Chosen Undead, who gained possession of Seath's fragment of the Lord Soul.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: The tide would turn in the Lords' favor when Seath, a pale dragon born without the scales of his kind, betrayed the dragons to ally with Gwyn, and pillaged their Primordial Crystal. Seath's lack of scales coupled with his vulnerability provided the Lords with a key piece of information: that the scales of his brethren were the source of their immortality. Gwyn thus used his Great Soul to manipulate the light of the sun, transforming rays of sunlight into lightning, a form of energy capable of penetrating dragon scales. Meeting the dragons in battle, Gwyn used his spears of sunlight to peel apart the dragons' scales, while his knights employed lightning-infused weapons to similar effect. The Witch of Izalith and her daughters weaved great firestorms, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons; while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons. Gwyn's eldest son would also take part in the war with his father, killing several dragons with his

title: Dragon
snippet:
The tide was turned when Seath the Scaleless betrayed his own kind, and sided with the Lords. For this he was awarded Dukedom, embraced by the royalty, and given a fragment of a great soul. The Lords were successful, and claimed dominion of the world.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A time-honored classic returning from the previous *Souls* games, the Moonlight Greatsword is a strong weapon in the hands of a dedicated Sorcery caster.

Unlike its previous iterations, *Dark Souls III*'s Moonlight Greatsword inflicts both physical and Magic damage, as well as being given scaling in Strength, albeit poorly. However, this does not change the fact that the physical scaling should be ignored, outside of meeting the minimum wielding requirements, in favor of leveling Intelligence, as the Moonlight Greatsword has been traditionally built (though as is the case with most melee weapons, it only scales effectively up to 40 in the offensive stats). The physical damage component is useful when performing criticals, as both damage types are magnified during the attack, allowing it to more easily punch through foes' flat Defenses.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Moonlight Greatsword uses the same moveset as the Greatsword of Judgment, utilizing horizontal and vertical slashes. However, it also has one of the longest reaches among greatswords, being beat only by the Wolf Knight's Greatsword and Onyx Blade. Its skill, Moonlight Vortex, charges the weapon for a powerful thrust attack that channels moonlight energy into a spear-like close-range attack to further augment its lethality. As such, this weapon is best utilized if the wielder equips heavy armor in order to utilize Poise, as is the case with all greatswords in the game.

Fully charging either the one- or two-handed strong attacks will unleash a wave of moonlight energy, at the cost of 4 Durability per use. The moonlight waves inflict only Magic damage; however, hitting an enemy with both the blade and the moonlight wave at close range will result in not only physical damage but also heavy Magic damage being dealt.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - second_phase 
 second_phase : Depleting the main Watcher's HP will trigger a cutscene, which shows the main Watcher absorbing power from the corpses around the arena. After this, the second phase of the battle commences.

At this point, the Watcher's sword will ignite, causing it to deal additional Fire damage and leaving trails in the floor that erupt into large pillars of flame. The Watcher himself will also take on an Embered appearance, revealing his true form as one of the Lords of Cinder.

The other Watchers no longer rise during the second phase, but the main Watcher is considerably more aggressive and powerful. The fight plays out in a similar fashion, but most of the Watcher's greatsword attacks are altered in some way. Killing the Watcher at this point will end the fight, but dying will reset it entirely, requiring the player to beat the first phase again.

title: Old Moonlight
snippet:
Old Moonlight -  Dark Souls III - spell - effect 
 effect : The caster conjures a Moonlight Sword with the staff and holds it ready. It can be released at any time, performing a crosswise horizontal slash like Soul Greatsword while also unleashing a moonlight wave like the Moonlight Greatsword. FP is only consumed upon releasing the attack, and the caster can move slowly with the sword at the ready or roll to cancel it. The spell is made up of two components, the Moonlight Sword and the moonlight wave; the Moonlight Sword inflicts 1.25 times the Spell Buff of the catalyst as Magic damage, while the moonlight wave deals 1.5 times the Spell Buff of the catalyst as Magic damage.

snippet:

title: Darkeater Midir
snippet:
The water in Midir's arena has a similar aesthetic to the sludge in Aldrich's, having various bones and pieces of flesh floating in it. Those corpses will bleed if struck with any weapon.
The water itself is able to be seen through, it looks as though the pool is deep, as one can see the supposed floor beneath it, meaning the player would be walking on the surface of the water itself.
The transition attack where Midir breathes fire and then blasts his dark beam may be an homage to *Shin Godzilla*, a fictional film monster.
The sorcery born from his soul, Old Moonlight, is possibly a nod to the earlier designs of the Moonlight Greatsword, as seen in Demon's Souls.
During his Abyssal flame breath attacks, it is possible to hear what resembles a human chorus amidst Midir's inferno. It is most audible at the encounter on the bridge, as there is no soundtrack and little ambient noise during this battle.

He uses the skills of both his ultra greatsword and greatshield frequently. During the fight, he tends to wield his ultra greatsword with both hands, performing powerful attacks with it.

title: Waterlogged
snippet:
Waterlogged -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Waterlogged** is a status effect in *Dark Souls II*.

It is contracted when standing in a Pharros' Contraption that fills an empty pool with healing water, or patches of water found in many areas of the game. The healing water slowly regenerates health as the player stands in it, and cures status effects like poison by allowing it to wash off. This effect also works like the Flash Sweat pyromancy, making the player far more resistant to fire attacks, at the cost of taking more lightning damage. The effect can also stack with Flash Sweat for even more fire defense.

In some areas of the game, this can occur automatically, such as traversing water itself, or during a rain storm. However, this will not regenerate the player's health, but instead only alter their elemental resistances. Care should be taken as to who or what the player is going to fight when the status effect is contracted.

title: Greatsword of the Forlorn
snippet:
Greatsword of the Forlorn -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Greatsword of the Forlorn is a very potent weapon, with the ability to deal massive damage in three different ways.

The weapon deals a great deal of both physical and Dark damage, as well as a good amount of Bleed build-up. This makes the weapon useful against most foes.

The weapon's main mechanic is that it, similarly to the Dark Pyromancy Flame and the Scythe of the Forlorn, scales with how hollow the player is. In human form, it will have an extremely low attack rating, while it will have a slightly above-average damage output when fully hollowed.

Its moveset is similar to that of the Charred Loyce Greatsword; however, two-handed light attacks are standard greatsword swings.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The fight is very simple and is similar to Ceaseless Discharge from the original *Dark Souls*. The main difference being the absence of any easy trick to defeat the King.

The player has little room to maneuver around the area, and may walk off or be thrown off the edge, causing an instant death. Due to his well-telegraphed attacks and long recovery times, there will be many openings for both healing and dealing damage. This means that the small area often becomes the main obstacle in this fight.

title: Giant Clam
snippet:
Giant Clam -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Giant Clams are an easy source of Twinkling Titanite, an otherwise expensive upgrade material. They can be farmed in Ash Lake and the Crystal Cave, where they can be respawned repeatedly.
Shooting an arrow into a Giant Clam's mouth will briefly stun it.
When encountering Seath the Scaleless for the first time, in the Crystal Cave, the fog wall is not present. This allows the clams the chance to enter the room that houses the boss fight, if the player tries to run past them. Seath's attacks can harm them, but they will still only attack the player, making the fight a fair bit more challenging.

title: Sen's Fortress
snippet: Amongthem the famous sorcerer Big Hat Logan who tried to reach the Duke's Archives to seek Seath the Scaleless's knowledge, the Undead Prince Ricard a legendary hero who wandered the lands in a fateful ill-conceived journey until he ended up Undead and in Lordran and the Knight King Rendal and his Balder Knights that attempted to seek the Lordvessel and restore the power of the Flame to save their country plagued by Undead.

title: Looking Glass Knight
snippet:
While offline, the NPC phantoms that the Looking Glass Knight summons range between a halberd-wielding or a greatsword-wielding phantom.
It is possible to stagger the Looking Glass Knight while he is summoning. If this happens, the Looking Glass Knight will cancel the summon and resume fighting the player.
Attacks that hit the shield on its left side will deflect and do no damage. Any form of magic (sorceries/pyromancies/miracles/hexes) will also be deflected.
The Looking Glass Knight is affected by Profound Still. The Knight will still attempt to use lightning attacks through its sword, but no lightning will come out. The player and summons can still be hit by the actual sword during these attacks.
After defeating the Looking Glass Knight, enemies will be able to charge into the arena from the previous area if the player ran past them on the way to the boss fight. This can catch players off guard and lead to a quick death after the boss fight officially ends.

title: White Dragon Breath
snippet:
White Dragon Breath -  Dark Souls - spell - description 
 description : Sorcery developed by Logan during his infatuation with Seath the Scaleless. Emit crystal breath of Seath the Scaleless.

Although it no longer causes curses, what madness caused old Big Hat to appropriate this frightful power of the ancient dragons?

title: Skeleton Lords
snippet:
Skeleton Lords -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : At the beginning of the fight, the player can dish out tons of damage and even kill one of the Skeleton Lords before they can even touch the ground to fight back.
The Skeleton Lords can be backstabbed and parried. They can also be knocked down with heavy, ground-slamming attacks.
The skeletons spawned during this fight are notoriously less aggressive than those found in other areas of the game. While they will still chase the player relentlessly, most of the time they will just linger around and only attack every now and then.
Spawned skeletons are able to parry and riposte.
All skeletons, including the bosses, are weak to Fire and Lightning.
Blue Sentinel members can buy Holy Water Urns from Targray for 300 souls, making this fight much easier.
The pillars in the room can easily block the Skeleton Lords' pyromancies.
By burning a Bonfire Ascetic on the Undead Lockaway bonfire, the Skeleton Lords can be respawned.

title: Light Crossbow
snippet:
Light Crossbow -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Light Crossbow is the weakest and lightest crossbow in *Dark Souls*. However, it is likely the first crossbow the player will obtain.

Like all crossbows, you cannot aim down sights so the Binoculars can help with aiming. With the Binoculars, line the target up in the exact center of the screen. Change to Light Crossbow without moving the camera, then fire. Like all crossbows, Light Crossbow does not scale off any stats though upgrading increases base damage, if infusing the AR of elemental bolts is added to the elemental AR of the infusion, which can be beneficial. Use ammo types that elementally match the infusion when possible and factor in enemy resistances when choosing an infusion and/or ammo type.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The Silver Pendant, although not required, can be of great help as it blocks his magic attacks if used with correct timing.

Great Grey Wolf Sif can help in this battle. Whilst Sif's attacks are not very damaging, the extra summon can keep Manus distracted and give the player time to heal. It is wise to only summon Sif after Manus is below half health, to distract him in his harder phase, making it less likely the player will be targeted by the Dark Orb barrage attack.

Sif's summon sign is *inside* the Manus's arena, directly to the left of where the player spawns. As a result, Sif can only be summoned *during* the fight. Thankfully, Sif is summoned instantly after touching the sign, without the usual white phantom-summoning animation. Since it is summoned during the fight it does not increase Manus' Hp.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : The Moonlight Greatsword is the *Dark Souls II* interpretation of the Moonlight Sword, which has appeared in every FromSoftware game since *King's Field*.

title: Gaping Dragon
snippet:
Gaping Dragon -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Being a Dragon, it is very susceptible to Lightning.
Staying at the Gaping Dragon's side and attacking its legs, moving only when it begins to walk or fly, can result in an easy victory.
Ranged attacks can prove useful, especially while the boss is performing a forward charge.
Be sure to kill the Channeler located on the highest floor above the arena to prevent it from casting ranged attacks during the boss fight. It does not respawn.
As long as care is taken with positioning, there is no need to block or dodge during the fight, making two-handed weapons an excellent choice for melee attacks.
Locking on can make evading the Gaping Dragon's attacks harder, as it reduces the speed at which the player can move away from the boss.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Due to Lucatiel's poor A.I., keeping her alive during boss fights can be difficult. However, the player can equip the Redeye Ring so that the boss focuses its attacks on the player. That way, the player will simply have to avoid the boss attacks while Lucatiel deals damage. Summoning another player is another good way for keeping her alive.
The player can use a Bonfire Ascetic in order to make both the area boss and Lucatiel respawn. It is recommended to do this with the Flexile Sentry, since Lucatiel's chances of survival are higher in this boss fight. Should Lucatiel survive a battle with a boss respawned with an Ascetic, the fight will count for the achievement/trophy.
If the player kills Lucatiel, her equipment will be sold by Merchant Hag Melentia, although this method voids the achievement/trophy for that New Game cycle.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Can be parried, riposted and backstabbed in both phases of the encounter.
The Watchers wake up based on a timer. Damage dealt has an effect on how many of them are active.
All Watchers are instantly killed when the first phase of the fight is finished.
The Abyss-corrupted (red-eyed) Watchers are capable of finishing off the main Watcher. This has no direct effect on gameplay, however.
If an enemy followed the player up to the fog door, it may attract the corrupted Watcher's attention and he will keep trying to attack it for the rest of the first phase, rendering him unable to help against the others.
The Watchers that resurrect in the first phase of the fight are actually the same two Watchers, they will resurrect on the spot where they were killed.

title: Benhart of Jugo
snippet:
He can then be found next to the bonfire, past the Dragonriders, in Drangleic Castle. He remarks on the discord of the land, before changing locations. He can then be summoned to assist with the Looking Glass Knight encounter.

Next, he will move to the ramparts, past The Pursuer boss fight area, in the Forest of Fallen Giants. He will state that he will assist the player in any challenge. He will then remark on the lineage of his weapon and its apparent hidden potential.

If the Ashen Mist Heart is possessed, he can be found in the Memory of Orro near his position on the ramparts. He can be summoned to fight the Giant Lord. This is also the spot were he will give the player his equipment if his questline has been completed.

Benhart drops the Bluemoon Greatsword upon death. If his sword is taken to Maughlin the Armorer, he will note that the sword is a fake; the true sword being the Moonlight Greatsword.

title: Old Moonlight
snippet:
Old Moonlight -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : A memory of an old sword found deep within Midir.
This sorcery uses souls to grant form to the thought, and attack with it.

Attacks are coupled with lightwaves, and sustaining the stance before attacking increases their speed and potency.

The sword is named after moonlight, but it is slightly different than the one fashioned of the paledrake Seath. Perhaps it is rooted in an older memory, from not long after the Beginning.

title: Moonlight Butterfly
snippet:
The Moonlight Butterfly's attacks are magic based. Wear light armor with high magic resistance (physical resistance is irrelevant), so you can dodge quickly and mitigate damage in case you get hit.
The butterfly spends most of the fight outside of melee range. While it's possible to defeat it using only melee weapons, players lacking ranged attacks (i.e., a bow or magic) are left to dodge (or block and heal) until it lands. A ranged weapon is therefore strongly advised, but not one that locks the player into long charge / reload animations (i.e., don't try to use a Heavy Crossbow), which would make it much harder to dodge the projectiles. The priority during the flight phases is to stay alive (and, ideally, take no damage at all).
During the flight phases, try to keep as far as possible (though within targeting range, naturally) to make it easier to identify and dodge the butterfly's attacks.

title: Crystal Ring Shield
snippet:
Crystal Ring Shield -  Dark Souls - shield - description 
 description : Weapon born from the mystical creature of the Darkroot Garden, the Moonlight Butterfly.

Imbued with a powerful crystal power, like the butterfly created by Seath the Scaleless. Can emit crystal light rings.

title: The Last Giant
snippet:
In the first half of the fight, the giant will use three main attacks, the first of which is a low sweep with its left arm. This attack is fairly easy to dodge and the wind up is noticeable. Roll between the giant's legs to get a few hits in before backing away. As the player is often right near a leg at this point, the follow up attack is usually a stomp with either foot. The third possible attack is a triple stomp, alternating feet while moving. Roll away to avoid getting crushed, and substantially stunned and damaged.

A semi-rare occurrence during the second part of the fight involves the giant falling forwards, instantly killing the player if he/she happens to be right below. If you are not caught in this, then it serves as a fantastic opportunity to attack. This is sometimes the Giant's first move in the fight, and the Giant can catch itself with both hands, or can land flat on its face, where it will remain motionless for more than a few seconds.

title: Old Moonlight
snippet:
Old Moonlight -  Dark Souls III - spell - trivia 
 trivia : Like the Moonlight Greatsword and its successors, Old Moonlight is modeled after the Moonlight Sword from *King's Field*. However, Old Moonlight's model is based more directly on the original, and this is reflected in the spell description.

title: Darkmoon Soldier (Greatsword)
snippet:
Darkmoon Soldier (Greatsword) -  Dark Souls - enemy - plot 
 plot : Darkmoon Soldier Juu guards the darkened Anor Londo. He either attacks or aids the player depending on if they're in the Darkmoon Covenant, if the player is summoned to the darkened Anor Londo, he and his companion Kei will fight alongside the player. If the player has killed Gwynevere however, they will be hostile.

title: Loyce Soul
snippet:
In shorter terms, the Loyce Souls start dropping much more regularly after the Charred Knights dropping a specific number of items.

The best way to farm the knights is during the fight against the Burnt Ivory King, as players will be backed up by any rescued Loyce Knights (as well as summons such as Lucatiel of Mirrah and Twiggy Shei), and also due to the fact that the Charred Loyce Knights themselves will spawn more frequently (roughly 10-11 per cycle depending on how long the portals remain open). Once enough Charred Loyce Knights have been slain and the Burnt Ivory King's portal appears, the player may egress from the arena via using the Aged Feather, and repeating the process as many times as necessary; if phantoms were summoned, be sure to use a Black Separation Crystal first. As these Charred Loyce Knights are treated as boss minions and not as spawned enemies, they will always appear during the boss fight no matter how many times they are killed.
